The land in question is stated to be 24 Marlas falling in Khasra No.2/1, 9/5, 19/1, 22/3 (0-19) and Khasra No.9/3 (0-5) in Village Machgarh, Tehsil Ballabgarh, District Faridabad.
The petitioners are stated to have constructed the residential house as well as the house for cattle.
The Award came to be passed on 29.07.2008.
The Rapat Roznamcha No.742 dated 07.08.2008 was duly entered into and the land was handed over to the beneficiary department, HSIIDC.
The amount of compensation of Rs.4,61,82,24,716/- was deposited for the land and structure and the disbursement is to the tune of Rs.4,53,78,76,070/-.
The supplementary Award of Rs.5,04,32,568/- is also stated to be lying deposited with the Land Acquisition Collector.

The balance amount of compensation is lying with the Reference Court for disbursement to the tune of Rs.2,99,16,078/- and it has also been mentioned that the compensation qua the land involved in the present petition has been lifted by the petitioners.
The compensation was further enhanced by the Court of Additional Sessions Judge and a further sum of Rs.43,14,858/- had been duly deposited in that Court.

sentences.text: further enhancement before the Reference Court as per the stand of the State and therefore, the petitioners are estopped from raising any challenge to the acquisition proceedings on that ground in view of the law laid down in Indore Development Authority (supra).

The relevant portion reads as under:-
"224.

Thus, in our opinion, the word "paid"
used in Section 24(2) does not include within its meaning the word "deposited", which has been used in the proviso to Section 24(2).

Section 31 of the Act of 1894, deals with the deposit as envisaged in Section 31(2) on being 'prevented' from making the payment even if the amount has been deposited in the treasury under the Rules framed under Section 55 or under the Standing Orders, that would carry the interest as envisaged under Section 34, but acquisition would not lapse on such deposit being made in the treasury.
In case amount has been tendered and the land-owner has refused to receive it, it cannot be said that the liability arising from non-payment of the amount is that of lapse of acquisition.
Interest would follow in such a case also due to non-deposit of the amount.

Equally, when the land-owner does not accept the amount, but seeks a reference for higher compensation, there can be no question of such individual stating that he 4 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120370-DB was not paid the amount (he was determined to be entitled to by the collector).
In such case, the land- owner would be entitled to the compensation determined by the Reference court."
7. Thus, nothing is to be adjudicated upon in the present petition.

Resultantly, the instant petition,
being devoid of any merit, stands dismissed.

(G.S. SANDHAWALIA)
 JUDGE  (MEENAKSHI I. MEHTA)
